headline: Ten major AI developers have agreed or promised to change how they handle personal data after scrutiny from Britain's privacy regulator, which says problems remain.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a regulator-announced set of commitments from ten major developers, but they are promises and the regulator says problems remain.
importance_line: People in the UK may get clearer explanations and easier ways to control how AI firms use their data, and the ten firms face continued monitoring, but these are commitments not proven changes and the regulator admits open problems such as personal data inside trained models.
summary: The Register reports that Britain's data protection regulator, the ICO, said on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI have made or promised changes after a supervisory programme begun in 2025, including clearer explanations of how personal data is used to train AI models, easier ways for people to use their data rights and tougher checks of safeguards. The ICO says it will monitor whether the firms deliver and that problems remain, such as personal data buried in trained models and how people can have it removed; it paused its work with xAI to pursue a separate formal investigation into the Grok chatbot.
notes: Read in full on The Register; the ICO announcement itself was not opened. Same announcement as C12-05; category set to LAW (regulation) instead of the SEC default.
